language_task: pick up the cup on the table, and hang it on the mug tree.
outcome_evidence: The robot lifts the light-blue cup and carries it toward the mug tree (frames 165–225, head and left_wrist). When the right gripper opens, the cup falls rather than remaining suspended (frames 340–355, right_wrist and left_wrist). It ends upright on the table beside the tree, with the gripper withdrawn (frames 385–405, head and both wrist cameras). This is a visibly failed hanging attempt, not merely unconfirmed completion.

failure_annotations.explanation: After successfully transporting the cup, the robot opens its gripper without securing the cup on a branch. The cup descends away from the branch in frames 340–355 (right_wrist and left_wrist) and settles on the tabletop beside the tree by frames 364–369 (left_wrist). The placement therefore fails to accomplish hanging; the precise handle-to-branch misalignment is not fully visible.
failure_annotations.recovery: Reacquire the upright cup, align its handle with an available branch, and lower it until the branch supports it before releasing and withdrawing. No human intervention appears necessary.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The cup falls a short distance onto the table and remains upright; no breakage, spill, or other meaningful damage is visible in frames 364–405.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: The cup remains accessible on the tabletop and the tree remains standing, so another acquisition and hanging attempt can begin without environmental resetting or human intervention.
